draft.title: The chain rule
card: A composite function has one function inside another, such as (3x + 1)⁵. The inner function is 3x + 1 and the outer function is the fifth power.
The chain rule says: if y = f(g(x)), then dy/dx = f'(g(x)) × g'(x). Differentiate the outer function and leave the inside alone, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.
Example: y = (3x + 1)⁵. The outer derivative is 5(3x + 1)⁴. The inner derivative is 3. So dy/dx = 5(3x + 1)⁴ × 3 = 15(3x + 1)⁴.
A common mistake is to forget the last step and leave out the derivative of the inside.
draft.remember: Differentiate the outside, keep the inside, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.

a.q: What is the derivative of y = (2x + 7)⁴?
a.why: The outer derivative is 4(2x + 7)³ and the inner derivative is 2, so dy/dx = 4(2x + 7)³ × 2 = 8(2x + 7)³. The option 4(2x + 7)³ is tempting, but it leaves out the multiplication by the derivative of the inside.

b.q: Find the gradient of y = (x² − 3)³ at x = 2.
b.why: dy/dx = 3(x² − 3)² × 2x = 6x(x² − 3)². At x = 2 this is 6 × 2 × (4 − 3)² = 12 × 1 = 12. Wait: the correct value is 12, so 24 comes from a slip in the multiplication.
b.clue: The inner derivative of x² − 3 is 2x, not 2.

problems.detail: The why for (b) contains a stray self-correction ('Wait: the correct value is 12…') that reads like a draft note and will confuse students. It also does not clearly explain how 24 arises, or why the other distractors (6, 3) are wrong.

proposal.title: The chain rule
card: A composite function has one function inside another, such as (3x + 1)⁵. The inner function is 3x + 1 and the outer function is the fifth power.
The chain rule says: if y = f(g(x)), then dy/dx = f'(g(x)) × g'(x). Differentiate the outer function and leave the inside alone, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.
Example: y = (3x + 1)⁵. The outer derivative is 5(3x + 1)⁴. The inner derivative is 3. So dy/dx = 5(3x + 1)⁴ × 3 = 15(3x + 1)⁴.
A common mistake is to leave out the derivative of the inside. To find the gradient at a point, find dy/dx first, then substitute the x value.
